    - Another one wanting steel. Everyone wants steel since the roads went bad. Nobody wants a copper fox any more. Well. What is it?
    - *Player*. Brindle says the grate is holding across the tunnel mouth. Of course it is holding. I made it. (A pause.) Good to hear, though.

    - *Player*. The spear came home dirtier than it left. Hatch says it did its work. That is the best thing anybody can say about a blade.

    - A thing you made and send away should have a name, so it knows it was wanted. I scratch it small on the tang, under the grip, where nobody looks. Nobody is meant to look. That is not the point.
    - The heron on my door is made of old hinges. The fox on the roof is copper off a burst boiler. The thing in the yard is chain and springs and has no name yet; it has not told me one. The fiddler on the corner of Lantern Square is mine too. Saffi sits on its knee. It does not mind.
    - Every Walkout Day I weld one and give it away. Last year a small iron cat for Perch's loft. That big grey cat of Perch's sleeps beside it now. Best review I ever had.
    - Hatch. Sixteen years ago Hatch walked in with a bent spear-head and would not leave until I straightened it. A month later, back again: a pair of hunting knives, please. I said I make foxes. Hatch said foxes do not skin rabbits.
    - Now Hatch tells everyone the whole trade was Hatch's idea. It was. I grumble about it daily. I would grumble more if the roads did not need it.
